text:
olivia: Quick sync: I think we have a correctness hole when snapshot loads, soft-evict (demote) and handoff interleave. could lead to read-after-write regressions.

raj: can you give the minimal repro?

olivia: sketch: txn W commits -> node A soft-evicts prefix (keeps tombstones) -> snapshot service produces snapshot S (missing W due to staleness) -> node B claims and loads S -> client R reads pre-W state.

maria: so snapshot staleness + demote race. we assumed snapshots were "fresh enough" but turns out demote is a stronger signal.

sahil: we have demote markers but snapshot loader doesn't consult them. loader just trusts manifest timestamp.

andrew: we do have transfer fences for explicit handoffs, but demote (soft-evict) is not an explicit transfer; it's a local hint. need durable coordination.

olivia: proposal A: emit per-prefix demote_fence counter persisted under /evict-fence/<prefix>. snapshot manifests include "residency_id" = fence counter observed at snapshot time. claimant validates snapshot.residency_id >= latest fence; otherwise it rejects snapshot and pulls deltas or rebuilds.

raj: implementation note: when loading snapshot, if manifest missing residency_id treat as 0. claimant queries fence key and compares. rejection path either run small delta apply or refuse and trigger full rebuild; prefer delta-first.

maria: alternative: have snapshotter subscribe to fence change stream and never produce snapshots older than current fence. that avoids rejects but adds complexity.

sahil: subscribing is nicer but coupling snapshot service to eviction churn could increase snapshot churn. and we still need a validation at claim time as an H/A safety net.

andrew: piggyback idea: include demote_fence bump in our lease-epoch advancement prewrite so we avoid additional writes. downside: epoch advance is heavier and sometimes delayed. per-prefix fence write is cheaper and more targeted.

olivia: we also need a backpressure/circuit breaker: if many snapshots are rejected concurrently we might storm delta fetches. plan: track snapshot_reject_rate and throttle reclaims with exponential backoff + prioritized delta queue.

raj: GC: fence keys must be gc'd when prefix is fully retired. also consider TTL for abandoned prefixes. add a GC job that sees manifest=DELETED && tombstones expired -> remove fence key.

maria: testing: chaos harness that injects snapshot lag + concurrent demote/claim, assert linearizability for reads after writes that committed before demote. add metric: snapshot_rejects_due_to_fence and delta_apply_latency.

ci-bot: perf run summary: 1000 demote/claim cycles, snapshot rejects 0.45%, median delta-apply 2.1ms, p95 5.9ms. full results: https://ci/reports/9765-evict-fence.

andrew: sounds acceptable. small ops write per demote likely fine. need a simple library to read/compare fence key atomically with claim.

sahil: also edgecase: overlapping demote+claim where claimant reads fence just before demote persists. require pre-claim observable barrier: claim must wait for fence write to be durable or bump. effectively claim path does: 1) read latest fence; 2) attempt to claim; 3) if claim succeeds re-check fence; if fence increased, abort load and retry using newer snapshot/delta.

olivia: ok I'll draft a short RFC: fence key schema, snapshot manifest residency_id field, claim validation algorithm, delta fallback flow, GC strategy, chaos tests, compatibility rules for older snapshots (missing residency_id => zero). plan: prototype next sprint.

maria: include migration notes: old snapshots considered stale if any fence > 0; consider rolling deploy of snapshotter+claimant.

raj: and include opplaybook: how to debug frequent snapshot rejects (metrics to inspect, queries to run).

olivia: noted. thanks team. I'll post RFC link later today. :rocket:
